full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the respondents herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.131 of 2001 in the Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia for declaration of title in the disputed property stating, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to Mouza-Mozompur under S.A. Khatian No.259 corresponding to Plot No.369 comprising an area of .37 acre land originally belonged to defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, in two annas share and defendant No.1, Atiar Rahman in 14 annas share. Defendant No.1 was the minor son of defendant No.2 and for his welfare, for want of money defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, herself and as natural guardian, mother of the minor son, defendant No.1 on 30.06.1969 A.D. transferred .0825 acre land in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor by a sub-kabala deed dated 30.06.1969 being No.8077. The possession of the transferred land was handed over by the vendor in favour of the purchaser and after purchase, the predecessor of the plaintiffs possessed that land and paid rent after mutation for more than 12 (twelve) years. The predecessor of the plaintiff, Sarwar Hossain's name has been correctly recorded against the suit land in the present RS record. In RS Plot No.4132, the suit land measuring .0831 acre was recorded primarily in the name of Sarwar Hossain, but subsequently defendant No.1 filed Other Class Suit No.69 of 1987 against Sarwar Hossain and others in respect of the entire land of suit of S.A. Khatian challenging the transfer deed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor, Sarwar Hossain, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia. The suit was dismissed on contest and against that dis-missal decree, defendant No.1 filed an Other Appeal No.219 of 1987 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia. After hearing, the appeal was dismissed affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and in this manner, the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs to the suit land remained intact. The further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant Nos.1 and 2 in collusion with the settlement officials including the suit land measuring .0825 acre along with .37 acre in SA Plot No.369 with other lands pre-pared a collusive RS Khatian in the name of defendant No. 1. On the basis of that wrong collusive RS record, the defendants on 26.01.2001 denied the title of the plain-tiffs' which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for declaration of their title. 

 16. In this respect, plaintiff No.9 while deposing as PW1 stated that the suit land appertaining to Mouza Mozampur under S.A Khatian No.259 originally belong to defendant Nos.1 and 2 and defendant No.2 is the minor son of defendant No.1 who for the purpose of maintaining his minor son (defendant No.2) sold out the suit property measuring .0825 acre in favour of his father on 30.06.1969. He further depoed that soon after such transfer, his father got possession in such land and paid rent after mutating his name in suit Khatian. PW1 further stated that Title Suit being No.69 of 1987 was filed against their predecessor's title document, i.e. Kabala deed No.8077 dated 30.06.1969 by the defendant, but they lost the same up to Appellate Court. During his course of examination, plaintiff No.9 produced their deed dated 30.06.1969, copy of R.S. Khatian No.330, rent receipt showing payment of rent, the DCR, copy of math porcha, copy of S.A Khatian No.259 along with the certified copy of judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.69 of 1987 and Title Appeal No.219 of 1987. All those documents were produced and being marked as exhibits in course of his examination. Waliur Rahman, PW2, deposed that he is the contagious land holder of the suit property and the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property for long term by erecting boundary wall. During his course of cross examination the aforementioned testimonies of the PWs were not shaken in any manner. On perusal of those evidence on record, we find that there is no intrinsic weakness and inherent infirmity in those testimonies. Thus, we are not in a position to disbelieve them.
